utterances.text: Would you also agree that mortars are mobile weapons, able to be generally moved and assembled for use with relative ease?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, that is the advantage of a mortar, mortar weapons system, as compared with artillery, is its flexibility, the ability to use it, and pack up and move and fire again relatively quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Are mortars easy to camouflage?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And am I correct in my recollection of our conversation yesterday that depending on the terrain you said that mortars fired from temporary positions leave very little trace behind of their use; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, your team prepared, as we heard, a report on your investigation into the shelling of 5 February 1994, setting out your findings; and that was completed around the 15th of that month?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we just have a look at P1441 again, please, and go over to page 9 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, is this, General - and we can scroll slowly through and go over then to page 10 and 11 - but while we read, perhaps I can ask the question: Is this, General, a copy of the final report done by your team at the time?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: It appears to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go to the following page, 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we have a technical error, I can certainly provide the general with an unmarked copy of P1441 and refer to the pages on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you have a copy -- I'm sorry, I overlapped. I was told that we or are now expecting some technical difficulties with the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Would my friend be able to assist me with a hard copy of P1441?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And when you receive this, unfortunately the pages aren't numbered, General, but I'd invite you to count over to pages 9, 10, and 11 just to confirm that you recognise the report.

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now -- thank you. Now, this report had several annexes, A to G, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And could you just continue flipping over to page 12 of the document in front of you and tell me if you see the annexes listed on page 12?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And what did those annexes comprise? Can you explain that to us, please.

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Do you want me to read the --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did those annexes --

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: -- or explain them?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did those annexes comprise your investigation as a whole?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And the final report that you've just seen was drafted based on the investigation as a whole and an analysis of the information contained in those annexes?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And I'd just like to put a couple of propositions to you based on your report. Could you confirm based on their investigation that your team concluded that the mortar bomb in question here had been launched in a conventional manner from 120-millimetre mortar tube?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that it exploded at ground level and didn't impact a market stall or a tabletop --

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: That's correct --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: -- on the way down?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that your team found the crater shape to be consistent with the normal impact of a mortar bomb on an asphalt surface?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And that your team assessed the direction of fire as being between 330 and 420 mils?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just a couple more things I'd like you to confirm from your report. Are you -- do you agree that there were UNMOs on the Bosnian side to the north-east of the impact area and that they were generally free to move about as they wished?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that on the Bosnian side there were no known fixed mortar positions along the direction of fire assessed by your team?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And your team did learn that in Bosnian Serb army-held territory that the assessed angle of fire or the directional bracket fell within the area of responsibility of the Kosevo Brigade of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And your team also had information that there were Bosnian Serb army mortar positions in the assessed direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: I don't recall positions, but I would have to go back and look at my -- look at the annexes to confirm --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we --

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: I recall one position within the bracket that we had identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I did misspeak. It was "a position" and not "positions." And are you also able to confirm that since October 1993 UNMOs had been denied freedom of movement to Bosnian Serb army positions in that assessed direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: I believe that to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And yesterday during our conversation you also said that neither you nor your team were given access to Bosnian Serb army-held territory in that assessed direction of fire, were you?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: I don't recall saying that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you recall -- can you confirm that your team had no access to Bosnian Serb-held territory in the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: I don't recall us not having access. I -- what I recall - and it's more -- it's my thinking now in relation to this - that we saw no need at the time to actually go into Bosnian Serb territory to try and find where the mortar might have been fired from.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And why did you see no need, General?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Because our expectation of being able to actually find something within the relatively large area that we had identified as being a possible firing point for the mortar, we judged to be very long, that we would actually be able to find something. It would be like trying to find a needle in a haystack, especially given that there was freshly fallen snow, that mortars, as I said earlier, don't necessarily leave tell-tale signs. And so unless it was a fixed position, it would be very difficult to actually find evidence of the mortar having been fired. Therefore, from our perspective going out to try and find evidence over this area we saw as being a little bit of a wild-goose chase and we did not engage in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have re-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Just indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I just have one question. Given what we have heard from the Prosecution, did anything emerge that might have changed the basic conclusions that you draw, especially with regard to responsibility, with regard to deciding which side actually fired the shell?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question. Did anything emerge -- do you mean since the investigation or during the investigation? If your question is whether or not I can recollect from the time of the investigation anything today that would cause me to come to a different conclusion, the answer would be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you for having come here to testify.

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, General Gauthier. On behalf of the Chamber I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. The hearing is now adjourned. Tomorrow we'll resume at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of October, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
